# Roofer | England | October 2026 — Evidence Pack

A fixture for the trade facts loader: a short pack in the generated layout, rows taken from Brandon's roofer run of October 2026 (the Perplexity output, exported as "Roofer England Evidence Pack – October 2026.pdf"). Not the full pack.

## TABLE A — Service process

| Service | Stages (4–8) | Materials and methods | Timing | Source(s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Roof repairs | 1. Inspect (from ground, loft, then roof access). 2. Identify cause (slipped or broken units, failed mortar, flashing, valley, underlay). 3. Set safe access (scaffold or short-duration ladder or roof ladder). 4. Replace like-for-like units, refix. 5. Repair flashings and valleys. 6. Check gutters and outlets. | Matching tiles or slates; mechanical fixing to BS 5534 on re-fixed units; lead to code per application. Listed buildings: matching like-for-like repairs generally do not need consent. | Varies; no standard. Ladders only for tasks measured in minutes. | HSE roof work; Marley maintenance; Historic England HEAG304 |
| Storm damage repairs | 1. Make safe and temporary weatherproofing (customer should speak to insurer first if possible). 2. Photograph or video damage. 3. Itemised invoice for emergency work. 4. Assess cause: storm or pre-existing wear and tear. 5. Quote permanent repair for insurer. 6. Permanent repair to BS 5534. | Temporary sheeting; replacement units; mechanical fixing. Insurer assesses whether storm conditions occurred, damage is consistent with storm, and storm was the main cause. | Varies; no standard. No fixed claim settlement timescale; insurers must handle claims "promptly and fairly". | ABI storm FAQ; ABI claims; FOS storm; FCA ICOBS 8.1 |
| Roof inspections | 1. External visual check (cracked, slipped, missing units). 2. Valleys, flashings, abutments. 3. Ridge and bedding mortar. 4. Gutters and downpipes. 5. Moss and lichen. 6. Loft check: daylight, torn underfelt, damp, condensation, ventilation. 7. Written condition report (for example before solar). | Visual and loft inspection; treat all roofs as fragile until confirmed otherwise. | Marley cites twice a year (spring and autumn) and after big storms: manufacturer advice, not a regulation. | Marley maintenance; ABI storm FAQ; NFRC homeowners guide |
| Dry ridge and dry verge | 1. Remove mortar-bedded ridge and verge. 2. Fix ridge batten or brackets. 3. Lay ridge roll or union with ventilation as needed. 4. Mechanically fix ridge and hip tiles. 5. Fit verge units to each course. 6. Check ventilation path. | Systems tested to BS 8612 (fixing resistance, weathertightness, durability, ventilation). Some systems not compatible with all decorative ridges. | Varies; no standard. | BSI BS 8612; Marley dry fix |
| Leadwork | 1. Select code for application. 2. Cut and dress lead; limit piece sizes. 3. Form soakers, step and cover flashings, aprons, valleys or flat lead bays. 4. Wedge and point into chases. 5. Patinate. | Rolled lead to BS EN 12588 (±5% thickness tolerance); design to BS 6915. Code 3 soakers; code 4 flashings, soakers, valleys; codes 5 to 8 flat and pitched roofing, gutters. | Varies; no standard. | BSI BS 6915; Midland Lead codes; Calder Lead |

## TABLE B — Signs and failure

| Service | Signs customer notices (3–5) | What fails when skipped (2–3, with mechanism) | What fails when done badly (2–3) | Source(s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Storm damage repairs | Tiles or slates on ground after high winds; visible gaps; water ingress during storm; displaced ridge | Delay in temporary repair → further water damage; no photos or invoice → weaker claim evidence | Repair that ignores pre-existing wear → insurer disputes cause; permanent work before speaking to insurer → claim complications | ABI storm FAQ; FOS storm |
| Roof inspections | Moss build-up; loose or missing pointing; gaps between tiles; light in loft; damp patches | Undetected defects become "wear and tear" not covered by insurance | Inspector walks fragile roof or rooflight → fall through; no loft check → condensation missed | ABI storm FAQ; HSE fragile |
| Dry ridge and dry verge | Cracked ridge mortar; ridge tiles loose or missing; mortar pieces in gutter; verge mortar falling out | Mortar ridge relies on bedding → wind uplift once mortar cracks | System not tested to BS 8612 or incompatible with ridge type → poor fixing and weathertightness | BSI BS 5534; BSI BS 8612; Marley dry fix |
| Leadwork | Split or holed flashing; damp around chimney; leaks at back gutter; lifted flashing | Split lead → water penetration at abutments | Lead back gutter not cleared → leaks; wrong code for use → premature failure (code chosen by application) | SPAB chimneys; Midland Lead codes |
| Flat roof replacement | Ponding that doesn't dissipate; sagging; splits; leaks; dirt or algae in ponded areas | Ponding → progressive deflection (25 mm over 20 m² ≈ 500 kg) → more ponding | Re-waterproofing alone doesn't fix ponding; backfalls → standing water; thin gutter insulation → surface condensation | LRWA GN7; ABI storm FAQ; Bauder BS 6229 summary |

## TABLE C — Rules and standards

| Rule or standard | Which services | What it requires | What customer has to do | Source URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Approved Document L vol 1 (2021 incl. 2023) | Roof replacement; Flat roof replacement | Renovation includes stripping to rafters or joists and rebuilding, and replacing the waterproof membrane on a flat roof. Renovated roof target 0.16 W/m²K; threshold 0.35; new roof elements 0.15; fallback to best U-value with ≤15-year simple payback, generally not worse than 0.7 after upgrade. | Notify or use a registered installer | AD L 2021 |
| Planning Portal guidance on re-covering | Roof replacement; Roof repairs; Flat roof replacement | No application normally if <25% of total building envelope AND <50% of roof affected. Approval needed if limits exceeded, structural alterations, significantly different fire performance, or new covering increases weight by 15% or more. | Nothing below limits; otherwise notify or apply or use a registered installer | Planning Portal |
| Competent person scheme — roof coverings (Sch 3 para 16) | Roof replacement; Tile/Slate roofing; Flat roof replacement | A registered installer self-certifies replacement roof coverings instead of a building control application. | Ask for the scheme certificate on completion | gov.uk CPS list |

## TABLE E — Facts

| Fact | Correct statement | Common wrong version | Source URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum tile pitch | Product-specific: concrete plain tiles 35°; clay plain 30° to 40°; Marley Wessex 15°; Ludlow Plus 22.5°. | "Tiles can go on any pitch above X°" (single figure). | Marley pitch; Marley Wessex; Marley Ludlow Plus |
| Mortar ridges | BS 5534 no longer relies on mortar tensile strength for wind uplift; ridge and hip tiles must be mechanically fixed. Mortar bedding is still recognised. | "Dry ridge is legally required" / "mortar-only ridges are compliant." | BSI BS 5534; Marley BS 5534; Marley dry fix |
| Moss | Low or moderate moss is not normally harmful; heavy build-up keeps the roof wetter and slows drainage. | "Any moss is destroying your roof." | Marley moss; NFRC GN58 |
| Nesting season | The law protects any wild bird nest in use or being built, whenever that is; gov.uk gives no fixed season dates. | "Nesting season is legally March to August, and work is fine outside it." | WCA s1; gov.uk wild birds |
